correctness.rationale: For s=y+2z and t=x+y+z, the allowed z are precisely max(0,s−t) through floor(s/2). Sorting by s modulo a gives the finite representation count. At the proposed G the first two rows give h+1 and p−h−1 and all later rows vanish. Each successor below G+a has the unique form G+aj−dv with 1≤v<a and j=ceil(dv/a)≥1; coprimality makes this a bijection with the nonzero offsets. The first two rows give p+j−δ, with δ the second-row saturation correction. If δ>0, the raw third-row count minus δ−j+1 is h−d+j−ceil(v/2)≥0, since d(a−v)/a<(a−v)/2. The nonnegative third-row count therefore supplies any deficit. At G+a the second row gains one entry even at the upper endpoint, giving at least p+1. Adding one a-coin then propagates the bound to every larger integer. The rechecked independent three-coin dynamic program (check_record4.py and check_record4_output.txt) found exactly p at all 30,750 boundaries and at least p+1 at all 1,940,622 successors for odd a≤83; it also found D(74)=8 and D(75),…,D(79)=9 for (5,3), which proves the stated out-of-range example by residue monotonicity. The supplied code and output are recorded corroboration, not an infinite proof or executed in this review.
